candidate_relations.reason: Rosai-Dorfman disease is a related histiocytosis but typically S100-positive with massive lymphadenopathy, unlike CD1a/S100-negative ECD.
Histiocytosis is the parent family and omits Erdheim-Chester disease with osteosclerosis, orbitopathy, and hairy kidney.
No granulomas were seen, so sarcoidosis is a different granulomatous disease.
Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis is a related non-Langerhans histiocytosis with incompatible skin-joint phenotype versus ECD.
Bone tumor is a generic parent for the osteosclerotic lesions and omits ECD.
Erdheim-Chester disease matches symmetric long-bone sclerosis, exophthalmos, perinephric thickening, and CD68+ CD1a− S100− foamy histiocytes.
Paget disease of bone is a remodeling disorder, not a foamy histiocytic infiltration.
Multifocal osteosclerotic histiocytosis is a descriptive synonym of the skeletal ECD pattern in this multisystem case.
Histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy denotes Rosai-Dorfman disease, an incompatible histiocytosis subtype.
Osteopetrosis is a diffuse sclerosing bone disease without histiocytic IHC of ECD.
Negative tumor markers and foamy histiocytes without malignancy exclude bone metastasis.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis is excluded by CD1a/S100/langerin negativity.
Skeletal sarcoidosis would show granulomas, which were absent.
